evidence.claim: The drive described here follows RM 337 from Camp Wood through Leakey to Vanderpool; the full numbered highway continues to Medina.
evidence.quote: Ranch to Market Road 337 (RM 337) is a ranch-to-market road in Real and Bandera counties in Texas, United States, that connects Texas State Highway 55 (SH 55) in Camp Wood with Texas State Highway 16 (SH 16) in Medina.

evidence.claim: The road began in 1945 as Farm to Market Road 337 between Camp Wood and Leakey.
evidence.quote: The route was first designated on June 11, 1945, as Farm to Market Road 337 (FM 337), traveling from Camp Wood to Leakey.

evidence.claim: Leaving Camp Wood, the road passes ranches and crosses Camp Wood Creek twice before climbing into the hills.
evidence.quote: leaving Camp Wood, the highway's route becomes rural and passes by many ranches and small subdivisions. RM 337 crosses Camp Wood Creek twice with the route traversing through hilly areas after the second crossing.

evidence.claim: It straightens onto flatter ground approaching Leakey, follows Sixth Street through town and crosses the Frio River near the city limits.
evidence.quote: RM 337 straightens out near John Buchanan Road and travels through a more flat area then enters the Leakey city limits near an intersection with Patterson Creek Road.

evidence.claim: More hills lead to RM 187 near Lost Maples State Natural Area.
evidence.quote: East of Leakey, RM 337 continues to travel through hilly areas for several miles before meeting RM 187 near the Lost Maples State Natural Area.

evidence.claim: The roads share about a mile before separating at Vanderpool, with the Sabinal River crossing just east of the junction.

evidence.claim: Cypress and cedar supported Leakey’s early lumber and shingle production along the Frio River.
evidence.quote: Anglo-American settlement of the area began in 1856 when John Leakey, his wife Nancy, and a few others settled near a spring along the banks of the Frio River. Shingles and lumber were produced from the abundant cypress and cedar trees.

evidence.quote: During the early 1900s, ranching superseded lumber, cotton cultivation, and corn production in importance to the local economy. The raising of Angora goats was a major component of the ranching industry.

evidence.claim: The road began in 1945 as Farm to Market Road 337 between Camp Wood and Leakey.
evidence.quote: The route was first designated on June 11, 1945, as Farm to Market Road 337 (FM 337), traveling from Camp Wood to Leakey.

evidence.claim: It became a ranch-to-market road in 1956. Extensions in 1957 and 1960 carried it farther east, and another eight miles brought it to RM 187 in 1968.
evidence.quote: It was redesignated RM 337 on October 1, 1956. On October 31, 1957, it was extended 6.5 miles (10.5 km) eastward, and on September 27, 1960, the route was extended another 3 miles (4.8 km) eastward. On October 1, 1968, the highway was extended eastward 8 miles (13 km) to RM 187.

evidence.claim: The last addition came in 1975, when the former FM 1336 between RM 187 and SH 16 became part of RM 337, completing the connection to Medina.
evidence.quote: On December 25, 1975, the former FM 1336 from SH 16 to RM 187 was redesignated as part of RM 337, adding 19.5 miles (31.4 km) to the route.

The town became the seat of Real County when the county was created in 1913 from parts of Edwards, Bandera and Kerr counties.
